# ggseg and aal atlases

## 1. Objectives

Creating a new ggseg package with the AAL atlases (AAL1, AAL2 and AAL3)  
https://ggsegverse.github.io/ggseg.extra/  

AAL1: 82 cortical + 8 subcortical + 26 cerebellar = 116 regions
AAL2: 86 cortical (orbitofrontal) + 8 subcortical + 26 cerebellar = 120 regions
AAL3: 90 cortical (anterior cingulate) + 50 subcortical (thalamus) + 26 cerebellar = 166 regions

The original ggseg3dAAL package had only 2*41 regions based on the AAL2 version and reported in https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28412442/ (see Supplementary Material 3).  
https://github.com/ggseg/ggsegAal  

Compared to AAL3 version:  
- Missing OFClat (31,32), N = 2  
- Missing Amygdala (45,46), N = 2  
- Missing Basal ganglia (75-82), N = 6  
- Missing Cerebellum (95-120), N = 26  
- Missing Thalamus subdivision (121-150), N = 30  
- Missing ACC subdivision (151-156), N = 6  
- Missing Subnuclei (157-170), N = 14 

ggseg3dAAL has also a problem with shifted region from 9 to 15 labels:  
https://github.com/ggseg/ggsegAal/issues/4#issuecomment-3588275084

People were asking for AAL freesurfer surface:  
https://github.com/faskowit/multiAtlasTT/issues/8

New ggseg extra procedure:  
https://github.com/ggsegverse/ggseg.extra  

Old ggseg extra procedure:  
The instruction for creating a subcortical atlas are here:  
https://ggseg.github.io/ggsegExtra/articles/createaseg.html
The command make_volumetric_2_3datlas has an issue (https://github.com/ggseg/ggsegExtra/issues/34).  

## 2. Anatomical surface reconstruction of colin27 

 Cortical representations will use the Colin27 surface:  
- Download the colin27 at 1mm resolution (https://www.bic.mni.mcgill.ca/ServicesAtlases/Colin27).  
- Register the colin27 to the single_subj_T1.  
- Process colin27 with recon-all to get the colin27 surface.  

```{bash, eval=F}
module load fsl/6.0.7
module load Freesurfer/8.1.0


# Estimate transform
flirt -in colin27_t1_tal_lin.nii -ref single_subj_T1.nii \
      -dof 6 -cost corratio \
      -omat mov2fix_rigid.mat
# Apply transform
flirt -in colin27_t1_tal_lin.nii -ref colin27_t1_tal_lin.nii \
      -applyxfm -init mov2fix_rigid.mat \
      -out colin27_t1_tal_lin_reg.nii

# recon-all
recon-all -i  /data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/raw/colins27/colin27_t1_tal_lin_reg.nii.gz -s colin27_t1_tal_lin_reg -all
```

## 3. Cortical and subcortical AAL parcellations

Create AAL parcellations for cortical regions by hemisphere, basal ganglia with contextual cortex, and cerebellum.  

### a. AAL3

Download AAL3v2 (https://www.gin.cnrs.fr/fr/outils/aal/):    

```{bash, eval=F}
################################################################################

module load fsl/6.0.7
module load Freesurfer/8.1.0
export SUBJECTS_DIR=/data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/freesurfer

# paths
AAL3ORIG="/data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/raw/aal3/"
AAL3DIR="/data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/raw/aal3_cortical_subcortical/"
mkdir $AAL3DIR

# images 2mm
AAL3SPM=${AAL3ORIG}AAL3v1.nii.gz
AAL3PARC=${AAL3DIR}AAL3v1_free.nii.gz
AAL3OUT_COR_MASK=${AAL3DIR}AAL3v1_cortex_mask.nii.gz
AAL3OUT_SUB_MASK=${AAL3DIR}AAL3v1_sub_mask.nii.gz
AAL3OUT_BG_MASK=${AAL3DIR}AAL3v1_bg_mask.nii.gz
AAL3OUT_CER_MASK=${AAL3DIR}AAL3v1_cer_mask.nii.gz
AAL3OUT_COR=${AAL3DIR}AAL3v1_cortex.nii.gz
AAL3OUT_L=${AAL3DIR}AAL3v1_cortex_L.nii.gz
AAL3OUT_R=${AAL3DIR}AAL3v1_cortex_R.nii.gz
AAL3OUT_SUB=${AAL3DIR}AAL3v1_sub.nii.gz
AAL3OUT_BG=${AAL3DIR}AAL3v1_bg.nii.gz
AAL3OUT_CER=${AAL3DIR}AAL3v1_cer.nii.gz
AAL3OUT_BG_CONTEXT=${AAL3DIR}AAL3v1_bg_context.nii.gz

# transform into freesurfer space
mri_vol2vol --mov ${AAL3SPM} --targ $SUBJECTS_DIR/colin27_t1_tal_lin_reg/mri/T1.mgz --regheader --o ${AAL3PARC} --interp nearest

# start with empty mask
fslmaths "$AAL3PARC" -mul 0 "$AAL3OUT_COR_MASK"
fslmaths "$AAL3PARC" -mul 0 "$AAL3OUT_SUB_MASK"
fslmaths "$AAL3PARC" -mul 0 "$AAL3OUT_BG_MASK"
fslmaths "$AAL3PARC" -mul 0 "$AAL3OUT_CER_MASK"

# Cortical regions
# N = 36+6+3 = 45 regions/hemisphere (no Cingulate_Ant anymore)
COR="1-34 37-74 83-94 151-156"

for s in $COR; do
  if [[ "$s" =~ ^[0-9]+-[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    a=${s%-*}
    b=${s#*-}
    fslmaths "$AAL3PARC" -thr $a -uthr $b -bin -add "$AAL3OUT_COR_MASK" "$AAL3OUT_COR_MASK"
  else
    fslmaths "$AAL3PARC" -thr $s -uthr $s -bin -add "$AAL3OUT_COR_MASK" "$AAL3OUT_COR_MASK"
  fi
done

# Subcortical regions
# N = 76 (no Thalamus anymore)
SUB="75-80 95-150 157-170"

for s in $SUB; do
  if [[ "$s" =~ ^[0-9]+-[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    a=${s%-*}
    b=${s#*-}
    fslmaths "$AAL3PARC" -thr $a -uthr $b -bin -add "$AAL3OUT_SUB_MASK" "$AAL3OUT_SUB_MASK"
  else
    fslmaths "$AAL3PARC" -thr $s -uthr $s -bin -add "$AAL3OUT_SUB_MASK" "$AAL3OUT_SUB_MASK"
  fi
done

# Basal ganglia regions
# N = 50 (no Thalamus anymore)
BG="75-80 121-150 157-170"

for s in $BG; do
  if [[ "$s" =~ ^[0-9]+-[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    a=${s%-*}
    b=${s#*-}
    fslmaths "$AAL3PARC" -thr $a -uthr $b -bin -add "$AAL3OUT_BG_MASK" "$AAL3OUT_BG_MASK"
  else
    fslmaths "$AAL3PARC" -thr $s -uthr $s -bin -add "$AAL3OUT_BG_MASK" "$AAL3OUT_BG_MASK"
  fi
done

# Cerebellum regions
# N = 26 
CER="95-120"
for s in $CER; do
  if [[ "$s" =~ ^[0-9]+-[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    a=${s%-*}
    b=${s#*-}
    fslmaths "$AAL3PARC" -thr $a -uthr $b -bin -add "$AAL3OUT_CER_MASK" "$AAL3OUT_CER_MASK"
  else
    fslmaths "$AAL3PARC" -thr $s -uthr $s -bin -add "$AAL3OUT_CER_MASK" "$AAL3OUT_CER_MASK"
  fi
 done

# clean binary masks
fslmaths "$AAL3OUT_COR_MASK" -bin "$AAL3OUT_COR_MASK"
fslmaths "$AAL3OUT_SUB_MASK" -bin "$AAL3OUT_SUB_MASK"
fslmaths "$AAL3OUT_BG_MASK" -bin "$AAL3OUT_BG_MASK"
fslmaths "$AAL3OUT_CER_MASK" -bin "$AAL3OUT_CER_MASK"

# apply masks (keep original values)
fslmaths "$AAL3PARC" -mas "$AAL3OUT_COR_MASK" "$AAL3OUT_COR"
fslmaths "$AAL3PARC" -mas "$AAL3OUT_SUB_MASK" "$AAL3OUT_SUB"
fslmaths "$AAL3PARC" -mas "$AAL3OUT_BG_MASK" "$AAL3OUT_BG"
fslmaths "$AAL3PARC" -mas "$AAL3OUT_CER_MASK" "$AAL3OUT_CER"
fslmaths "$AAL3OUT_COR_MASK" -add "$AAL3OUT_BG" "$AAL3OUT_BG_CONTEXT"
fslmaths "$AAL3OUT_COR_MASK" -add "$AAL3OUT_CER" "$AAL3OUT_CER_CONTEXT"

# right hemisphere
fslmaths "$AAL3OUT_COR" -rem 2 -add 1 -uthr 1 -bin -mas "$AAL3OUT_COR_MASK" -mul "$AAL3OUT_COR" "$AAL3OUT_R"

# left hemisphere
fslmaths "$AAL3OUT_COR" -rem 2 -add 1 -thr 2 -uthr 2 -bin -mas "$AAL3OUT_COR_MASK" -mul "$AAL3OUT_COR" "$AAL3OUT_L"

################################################################################
```

### c. AAL1

Download AAL1 (https://www.gin.cnrs.fr/fr/outils/aal/):  

Converting the original AAL1 with four number to two numbers labels:

```{bash, eval=F}
################################################################################

module load fsl/6.0.7

# Répertoire contenant l'AAL1 original
AAL1ORIG="/data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/raw/aal/"

ATLAS="${AAL1ORIG}/ROI_MNI_V4.nii"
LUT="${AAL1ORIG}/ROI_MNI_V4.txt"

OUT="${AAL1ORIG}/AAL1_116.nii.gz"
OUTLUT="${AAL1ORIG}/AAL1_116.txt"

# Initialise le nouvel atlas à zéro
fslmaths "$ATLAS" -mul 0 "$OUT"

# Initialise la nouvelle LUT
> "$OUTLUT"

i=1

while read -r abbrev name oldcode
do
    # Ignore les lignes vides
    [ -z "$oldcode" ] && continue

    echo "$oldcode -> $i   $name"

    # Sélection exacte du label original
    fslmaths "$ATLAS" \
        -thr "$oldcode" \
        -uthr "$oldcode" \
        -bin \
        -mul "$i" \
        "${AAL1ORIG}/tmp_label"

    # Ajout au nouvel atlas
    fslmaths "$OUT" \
        -add "${AAL1ORIG}/tmp_label" \
        "$OUT"

    # Nouvelle LUT :
    # nouveau_code  nom  ancien_code
    printf "%d\t%s\t%d\n" \
        "$i" "$name" "$oldcode" >> "$OUTLUT"

    i=$((i+1))

done < "$LUT"

# Nettoyage
rm -f "${AAL1ORIG}/tmp_label.nii.gz"

echo
echo "Atlas créé : $OUT"
echo "LUT créée   : $OUTLUT"
echo "Nombre de labels : $((i-1))"

echo
echo "Plage des valeurs :"
fslstats "$OUT" -R
# 0.000000 116.000000

################################################################################
```

## 4. Color tables

There is not official lut for AAL. The aal version from MRICro (https://people.cas.sc.edu/rorden/mricro/mricro.html) has a lut for the AAL1 version. It will be adapted for the AAL1, AAL2 and AAL3.  

**read_palette_lut.py**
```{python, eval=F}
################################################################################
from pathlib import Path

lut_path = Path("aal.lut")
b = lut_path.read_bytes()
assert len(b) == 768, f"Expected 768 bytes, got {len(b)}"

R = b[0:256]
G = b[256:512]
B = b[512:768]

# color for region index i (0..255):
def color(i):
    return (R[i], G[i], B[i])

for i in range(1, 117):
    print(i, color(i))
################################################################################
```

## 5. Projecting  cortical labels

- Project AAL3 parcellation on the cortical colins surface.  
- After testing, projecting using projfrac 0.1 seems a reasonable compromise.  

### a. AAL3 

```{bash, eval=F}
################################################################################

module load fsl/6.0.7
module load Freesurfer/8.1.0
source $FREESURFER_HOME/SetUpFreeSurfer.sh
export SUBJECTS_DIR=/data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/freesurfer

AAL3=AAL3v1
AAL3DIR="/data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/raw/aal3_cortical_subcortical/"
AAL3OUT_L=${AAL3DIR}${AAL3}_cortex_L.nii.gz
AAL3OUT_R=${AAL3DIR}${AAL3}_cortex_R.nii.gz

SUBJ=colin27_t1_tal_lin_reg

CTAB=${AAL3DIR}${AAL3}_cortex.ctab

SURF_MGH_LH="$SUBJECTS_DIR/$SUBJ/surf/lh.${AAL3}.mgh"
OUTDIR_NUM_LH="$SUBJECTS_DIR/$SUBJ/label/${AAL3}_num_lh"
OUTDIR_NAM_LH="$SUBJECTS_DIR/$SUBJ/label/${AAL3}_lh"

SURF_MGH_RH="$SUBJECTS_DIR/$SUBJ/surf/rh.${AAL3}.mgh"
OUTDIR_NUM_RH="$SUBJECTS_DIR/$SUBJ/label/${AAL3}_num_rh"
OUTDIR_NAM_RH="$SUBJECTS_DIR/$SUBJ/label/${AAL3}_rh"

# Create label folders
mkdir -p "$OUTDIR_NUM_LH" "$OUTDIR_NAM_LH" "$OUTDIR_NUM_RH" "$OUTDIR_NAM_RH"

# project AAL3 volume to left surface
mri_vol2surf \
  --src $AAL3OUT_L \
  --regheader $SUBJ \
  --hemi lh \
  --surf white \
   --projfrac 0.1 \
  --interp nearest \
  --out $SURF_MGH_LH

# Reporting segmentation
mri_segstats --seg $SURF_MGH_LH --sum segstats.txt
# N = 46 (45 + background)

# Extract numeric labels for the left hemisphere
for id in $(seq 1 170); do
  mri_vol2label \
    --i "$SURF_MGH_LH" \
    --surf "$SUBJ" lh white \
    --id "$id" \
    --l "$OUTDIR_NUM_LH/lh.${AAL3}_${id}.label"
done
ls $OUTDIR_NUM_LH/ | wc
# N = 45

# rename left labels
while read -r id name r g b a; do
    src="$OUTDIR_NUM_LH/lh.${AAL3}_${id}.label"
    dst="$OUTDIR_NAM_LH/lh.${name}.label"
    if [ -f "$src" ] && [ "$(wc -l < "$src")" -gt 2 ]; then
      cp "$src" "$dst"
    fi
  done < <(awk 'NF>=6 && $1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ {print $1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6}' "$CTAB")

# project AAL3 volume to right surface
mri_vol2surf \
  --src $AAL3OUT_R \
  --regheader $SUBJ \
  --hemi rh \
  --surf white \
   --projfrac 0.1 \
  --interp nearest \
  --out $SURF_MGH_RH

# Reporting segmentation
mri_segstats --seg $SURF_MGH_RH --sum segstats.txt
# N = 46 (45 + background)

# Extract numeric labels for the right hemisphere
for id in $(seq 1 170); do
  mri_vol2label \
    --i "$SURF_MGH_RH" \
    --surf "$SUBJ" rh white \
    --id "$id" \
    --l "$OUTDIR_NUM_RH/rh.${AAL3}_${id}.label"
done
ls $OUTDIR_NUM_RH/ | wc
# N = 45

# rename right labels
while read -r id name r g b a; do
    src="$OUTDIR_NUM_RH/rh.${AAL3}_${id}.label"
    dst="$OUTDIR_NAM_RH/rh.${name}.label"
    if [ -f "$src" ] && [ "$(wc -l < "$src")" -gt 2 ]; then
      cp "$src" "$dst"
    fi
  done < <(awk 'NF>=6 && $1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ {print $1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6}' "$CTAB")
  
################################################################################
```

- Creating annotation files:  

```{bash, eval=F}
################################################################################

# left hemisphere
mris_label2annot \
    --s "$SUBJ" \
    --h  lh \
    --a ${AAL3} \
    --ctab "$CTAB" \
    --ldir "$OUTDIR_NAM_LH" \
    --nhits "$SUBJECTS_DIR/$SUBJ/label/lh.${AAL3}.nhits.mgh"
# Found 10095 unmapped vertices out of 169628


# right hemisphere
mris_label2annot \
    --s "$SUBJ" \
    --h  rh \
    --a ${AAL3} \
    --ctab "$CTAB" \
    --ldir "$OUTDIR_NAM_RH" \
    --nhits "$SUBJECTS_DIR/$SUBJ/label/rh.${AAL3}.nhits.mgh"
# Found 10076 unmapped vertices out of 168312

################################################################################
```

## 6. Cortical morphological operations 

Different morphological operations to closes holes and smooth borders of the labels.   
Notes: Background is -1 in freesurfer.  

Recipe:  
1. border smooth  
2. remove isolated island  
3. close background hole  

Notes: Part of the OFClat_L is replaced by Frontal_Mid_2_L 

```{bash, eval=F}
################################################################################

conda create -n meshing python=3.10
conda activate meshing
pip install nibabel
pip install numpy
pip install skimage
pip install trimesh

conda activate meshing
ipython 

################################################################################
```

Python functions:  
```{python, eval=F}
################################################################################

import numpy as np
from nibabel.freesurfer.io import read_annot, write_annot, read_geometry
from collections import deque

# Build vertex neighbors (mesh adjacency)
def mesh_neighbors(n_verts, faces):
    neigh = [set() for _ in range(n_verts)]
    for tri in faces:
        a, b, c = tri
        neigh[a].update([b, c])
        neigh[b].update([a, c])
        neigh[c].update([a, b])
    return [np.fromiter(s, dtype=np.int64) for s in neigh]

# Border smooth
# This keeps interiors unchanged and only rounds jagged edges.
def border_smooth(labels, neigh, n_iter=3, background=-1, keep_background=False,majority=0.60, min_votes=3):
    lab = labels.copy()
    for _ in range(n_iter):
        new = lab.copy()
        # boundary vertices = at least one neighbor with different label
        is_boundary = np.zeros(lab.size, dtype=bool)
        for v, nb in enumerate(neigh):
            if nb.size == 0:
                continue
            is_boundary[v] = np.any(lab[nb] != lab[v])
        for v in np.where(is_boundary)[0]:
            vals = lab[neigh[v]]

            if not keep_background:
                vals = vals[vals != background]
                if vals.size == 0:
                    continue
            # include self-label to stabilize borders
            vals = np.r_[vals, lab[v]]
            uniq, cnt = np.unique(vals, return_counts=True)
            k = np.argmax(cnt)
            winner, votes = uniq[k], cnt[k]
            # conservative update: only if strong agreement
            if votes >= max(min_votes, int(np.ceil(majority * vals.size))):
                new[v] = winner
        if np.array_equal(new, lab):
            break
        lab = new
    return lab

# only the biggest component per label
def keep_largest_component_per_label(labels, neigh, background=-1):
    lab = labels.copy()
    n = lab.size

    # Process each label separately
    for L in np.unique(lab):
        if L == background:
            continue

        # find all components of label L
        visited = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
        comps = []

        for seed in np.where(lab == L)[0]:
            if visited[seed]:
                continue
            # BFS for this component
            stack = [int(seed)]
            visited[seed] = True
            comp = []

            while stack:
                v = stack.pop()
                if lab[v] != L:
                    continue
                comp.append(v)
                for u in neigh[v]:
                    u = int(u)
                    if not visited[u] and lab[u] == L:
                        visited[u] = True
                        stack.append(u)

            if comp:
                comps.append(comp)

        if len(comps) <= 1:
            continue

        # keep only the biggest component
        comps.sort(key=len, reverse=True)
        keep = set(comps[0])

        # relabel the other components using dominant boundary neighbor label
        for comp in comps[1:]:
            comp_set = set(comp)

            boundary_neighbor_labels = []
            for v in comp:
                nb = neigh[v]
                out = nb[~np.isin(nb, list(comp_set))]
                if out.size:
                    boundary_neighbor_labels.append(lab[out])

            if not boundary_neighbor_labels:
                continue

            boundary_neighbor_labels = np.concatenate(boundary_neighbor_labels)
            boundary_neighbor_labels = boundary_neighbor_labels[
                (boundary_neighbor_labels != background) & (boundary_neighbor_labels != L)
            ]
            if boundary_neighbor_labels.size == 0:
                lab[np.array(comp, dtype=int)] = background
                continue

            uniq, cnt = np.unique(boundary_neighbor_labels, return_counts=True)
            newL = uniq[np.argmax(cnt)]
            lab[np.array(comp, dtype=int)] = newL

    return lab

# Close small background holes
def voronoi_fill_background_limited(labels, neigh, background=-1, max_dist=5):
    lab = labels.copy()
    n = lab.size

    dist = np.full(n, -1, dtype=np.int32)
    out  = lab.copy()

    q = deque()

    # initialize queue with non-background vertices
    for v in np.where(lab != background)[0]:
        dist[v] = 0
        q.append(int(v))

    # multi-source BFS with distance limit
    while q:
        v = q.popleft()
        if dist[v] >= max_dist:
            continue

        for u in neigh[v]:
            u = int(u)
            if dist[u] == -1 and lab[u] == background:
                dist[u] = dist[v] + 1
                out[u] = out[v]
                q.append(u)

    return out
  
################################################################################
```

### a. AAL3

Python final AAL3 recipe:  
```{python, eval=F}
################################################################################

aalversion = "AAL3v1"

fsdir = "/data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/freesurfer/colin27_t1_tal_lin_reg"

# left hemisphere

# read original annot and white surface
labels, ctab, names = read_annot(
    f"{fsdir}/label/lh.{aalversion}.annot"
)
verts, faces = read_geometry(
    f"{fsdir}/surf/lh.white"
)

# smoothing
neigh = mesh_neighbors(len(labels), faces)
labels_border = border_smooth(
    labels, neigh, n_iter=10, background=-1, majority=0.5
)

# keep biggest ones
neigh_border = mesh_neighbors(len(labels_border), faces)
labels_keep = keep_largest_component_per_label(
    labels_border, neigh_border, background=-1
)

# closing holes
neigh_keep = mesh_neighbors(len(labels_keep), faces)
labels_fill = voronoi_fill_background_limited(
    labels_keep, neigh_keep, background=-1, max_dist=5
)

write_annot(
    f"{fsdir}/label/lh.{aalversion}_recipe.annot",
    labels_fill, ctab, names
)


# right hemisphere

# read original annot and white surface
labels, ctab, names = read_annot(
    f"{fsdir}/label/rh.{aalversion}.annot"
)
verts, faces = read_geometry(
    f"{fsdir}/surf/rh.white"
)

# smoothing
neigh = mesh_neighbors(len(labels), faces)
labels_border = border_smooth(
    labels, neigh, n_iter=10, background=-1, majority=0.5
)

# keep biggest ones

)
```

## 7. ggseg procedure

Atlas creation with the ggseg.extra package:  
https://ggsegverse.github.io/ggseg.extra/ 

### a. Set environment

```{bash, eval=F}
################################################################################
# create conda environment (only once)

conda create -n ggseg python=3.10
conda activate ggseg

# R version
conda install -c conda-forge r-base=4.4

# ggseg.extra dependencies
conda install -c conda-forge \
  udunits2 \
  r-units \
  r-sf \
  r-rmapshaper \
  openssl \
  r-terra \
  freetype \
  fontconfig \
  harfbuzz \
  fribidi \
  pkg-config \
  r-pkgdown
  
################################################################################
module load fsl/6.0.7
module load Freesurfer/8.1.0
export SUBJECTS_DIR=/data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/freesurfer

conda activate ggseg

# rstudio
alias rstudio='/srv/shares/softs/rstudio-2026.01.0+392/rstudio --disable-gpu'

################################################################################
```

### b. R packages

```{r, eval=F}
################################################################################
# Packages for R-4.4.3

options(
  repos = c(
    ggsegverse = "https://ggsegverse.r-universe.dev",
    CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"
  )
)

install.packages("ggseg")
install.packages("ggseg3d")
install.packages("ggseg.formats")
install.packages("ggseg.extra")
install.packages("ggseg.docs")
install.packages("quarto")
install.packages("nanonext")

install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("muschellij2/freesurfer")
pak::pak("ggsegverse/ggseg.docs")

################################################################################
```

```{r, eval=F}
################################################################################
```

## 8. Package documentation and validation

This section describes how to validate the generated `ggsegAAL` package,
install it locally, generate the GitHub README, and build the pkgdown website.

The package is built by `04_package.R`. The following operations do not
rebuild the atlases.

### a. Validate package

Run the automated tests and R CMD check before publication.

```{r package-validation, eval=FALSE}
pkg <- "/data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/ggsegAal"

devtools::test(pkg)
devtools::check(pkg)
```

The tests verify the integrity and expected region counts of the nine
AAL atlas components.

Expected region counts:

| Atlas | Cortical | Subcortical | Cerebellum | Total |
|:------|---------:|------------:|-----------:|------:|
| AAL1  | 82       | 8           | 26         | 116   |
| AAL2  | 86       | 8           | 26         | 120   |
| AAL3  | 90       | 50          | 26         | 166   |

### b. Install package locally

Install the newly generated package in the active R library.

```{r package-install, eval=FALSE}
pkg <- "/data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/ggsegAal"

devtools::install(
  pkg = pkg,
  upgrade = FALSE,
  dependencies = FALSE
)

library(ggsegAAL)

packageVersion("ggsegAAL")
find.package("ggsegAAL")
```

Installation is necessary for the README examples because Quarto executes
R code in a separate session.

### c. Generate GitHub README

Generate the README.md from README.qmd  

```{r readme-generation, eval=FALSE}
pkg <- "/data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/ggsegAal"

quarto::quarto_render(
  input = readme_target,
  output_format = "gfm"
)
```

### d. Build pkgdown website

Build and preview the documentation website:

```{r pkgdown-build, eval=FALSE}
pkgdown::build_site(
  pkg,
  preview = TRUE
)
```

The website is generated in:

`/data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/ggsegAal/docs/`

The website uses the `ggseg.docs` template and includes the README,
package reference pages, and documentation for `ggseg3d_aal()`.


## 9. GitHub publication

This section describes how to publish `ggsegAAL` on GitHub and deploy
the pkgdown website using GitHub Pages.

Repository:

https://github.com/lemaitreh/ggsegAal

Documentation website:

https://lemaitreh.github.io/ggsegAal/

### a. Create GitHub repository

On GitHub, open:

https://github.com/new

Configure:

- Owner: `lemaitreh`
- Repository name: `ggsegAal`
- Description: `Automated Anatomical Labeling atlases for ggsegverse`
- Visibility: **Public**

Do not initialize the repository with a README, `.gitignore`, or license,
as these files are already managed locally.

Click **Create repository**.

### b. Create GitHub Personal Access Token

On GitHub:

**Settings ? Developer settings ? Personal access tokens
? Fine-grained tokens ? Generate new token**

Configure:

- Repository access: `Only select repositories`
- Selected repository: `ggsegAal`
- Repository permission / Contents: `Read and write`
- Expiration: according to your preference

Alternatively, a classic token with the `repo` scope can be used.

Save the token securely. It replaces the GitHub account password
when using Git over HTTPS.

### c. Initialize Git in RStudio

Open the package directory in RStudio:

`/data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/ggsegAal`

Then select:

**Tools ? Version Control ? Project Setup... ? Git**

Alternatively, open the RStudio terminal and run:

```{bash git-init, eval=FALSE}
cd /data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/ggsegAal

git status
```

If the directory is not already a Git repository:

```{bash git-init-new, eval=FALSE}
git init
git branch -M main
```

If Git is already initialized, do not run `git init` again.
Check the current branch with `git branch --show-current`.

### d. Connect the local repository to GitHub

In the RStudio terminal:

```{bash git-remote, eval=FALSE}
cd /data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/ggsegAal

git remote add origin https://github.com/lemaitreh/ggsegAal.git

git remote -v
```

If `origin` already exists, update its URL instead:

```{bash git-remote-update, eval=FALSE}
git remote set-url origin https://github.com/lemaitreh/ggsegAal.git
```

### e. Commit and push the package

Before publishing, verify that the repository contains no confidential
data, temporary files, or unnecessary generated outputs.

Also verify that `docs/`, `README.md` and the README figures under
`man/figures/` are not excluded by `.gitignore`.

In the RStudio terminal:

```{bash git-first-push, eval=FALSE}
cd /data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/ggsegAal

git add .
git status

git commit -m "Initial release ggsegAAL 3.0.0"

git push -u origin main
```

When prompted by GitHub:

- Username: `lemaitreh`
- Password: paste the GitHub Personal Access Token.

If the repository uses the `master` branch, replace `main` with `master`.

### f. Enable GitHub Pages

On GitHub, open the repository:

https://github.com/lemaitreh/ggsegAal

Navigate to:

**Settings ? Pages ? Build and deployment**

Configure:

- Source: **Deploy from a branch**
- Branch: `main`
- Folder: `/docs`

Click **Save**.

Once deployment is complete, the documentation website should be
available at:

https://lemaitreh.github.io/ggsegAal/

### g. Update the GitHub repository

After changing the README, package documentation or pkgdown website,
regenerate the affected outputs locally and commit the changes.

In the RStudio terminal:

```{bash git-update, eval=FALSE}
cd /data/extra/hlemaitre/aal/ggsegAal

git status
git add .
git commit -m "Update ggsegAAL documentation"
git push
```

A new commit is necessary only when files have actually changed.

### h. Important:
